_howto: Landmark papers from the fellowship journal club, grouped by session. Each entry: week, session title, topic, short title, citation, one-line finding, path to the PDF in public/files/articles/, and DOI where the PDF carried one. Add new papers by appending an entry and uploading the PDF.

articles.title: ARMA: low tidal volume ventilation in ARDS
articles.citation: ARDS Network. N Engl J Med. 2000.
articles.finding: 6 mL/kg predicted body weight versus 12 mL/kg: mortality 31% versus 40%. The foundation of lung-protective ventilation.

articles.session: ARDS: definition and protective ventilation beyond ARDS
articles.title: IMPROVE: intraoperative lung-protective ventilation
articles.citation: Futier E, et al. N Engl J Med. 2013.
articles.finding: Low tidal volume, PEEP, and recruitment during abdominal surgery reduced postoperative pulmonary complications.

articles.session: ARDS: definition and protective ventilation beyond ARDS
articles.title: PReVENT: low versus intermediate tidal volume without ARDS
articles.citation: Simonis FD, et al. JAMA. 2018.
articles.finding: In ventilated patients without ARDS, 6 versus 10 mL/kg made no difference to ventilator-free days.

articles.session: ARDS: definition and protective ventilation beyond ARDS
articles.title: The Berlin definition of ARDS
articles.citation: ARDS Definition Task Force. JAMA. 2012.
articles.finding: Replaced the 1994 AECC definition with mild, moderate, and severe categories by PaO2/FiO2 on PEEP of at least 5.

articles.title: ART: lung recruitment and titrated PEEP
articles.citation: Cavalcanti AB, et al. JAMA. 2017.
articles.finding: Aggressive recruitment maneuvers with PEEP titration increased 28-day mortality compared with low PEEP.

articles.title: EPVent-2: esophageal pressure-guided PEEP
articles.citation: Beitler JR, et al. JAMA. 2019.
articles.finding: Esophageal pressure-guided PEEP was no better than an empiric high PEEP-FiO2 table for death or ventilator-free days.

articles.title: LaSRS: methylprednisolone for persistent ARDS
articles.citation: Steinberg KP, et al. N Engl J Med. 2006.
articles.finding: No 60-day mortality benefit, more ventilator-free days early, and higher mortality when started after day 14.

articles.title: ACURASYS: cisatracurium in early severe ARDS
articles.citation: Papazian L, et al. N Engl J Med. 2010.
articles.finding: 48 hours of cisatracurium improved adjusted 90-day survival and ventilator-free days without more weakness.

articles.title: FACTT: conservative versus liberal fluid management
articles.citation: Wiedemann HP, et al. N Engl J Med. 2006.
articles.finding: Conservative fluids improved oxygenation and ventilator-free days with no difference in mortality or dialysis.

articles.title: FACTT: pulmonary artery versus central venous catheter
articles.citation: Wheeler AP, et al. N Engl J Med. 2006.
articles.finding: PAC-guided management did not improve survival or organ function and doubled catheter complications.

articles.title: ROSE: early neuromuscular blockade in ARDS
articles.citation: Moss M, et al. N Engl J Med. 2019.
articles.finding: Early cisatracurium with deep sedation versus usual care with light sedation: no difference in 90-day mortality.

articles.session: ARDS: proning and inhaled nitric oxide
articles.title: Inhaled nitric oxide in ARDS: meta-analysis
articles.citation: Adhikari NKJ, et al. Crit Care Med. 2014.
articles.finding: Inhaled nitric oxide improves oxygenation but does not reduce mortality at any severity of ARDS.

articles.session: ARDS: proning and inhaled nitric oxide
articles.title: PROSEVA: prone positioning in severe ARDS
articles.citation: Guerin C, et al. N Engl J Med. 2013.
articles.finding: Prone sessions of at least 16 hours in PaO2/FiO2 under 150 cut 28-day mortality from 33% to 16%.

articles.session: ARDS: proning and inhaled nitric oxide
articles.title: Prone positioning in acute respiratory failure
articles.citation: Gattinoni L, et al. N Engl J Med. 2001.
articles.finding: Proning improved oxygenation but not survival. Post hoc, the sickest quartile appeared to benefit, which set up PROSEVA.

articles.session: ARDS: proning and inhaled nitric oxide
articles.title: Prone-Supine II: proning in moderate and severe ARDS
articles.citation: Taccone P, et al. JAMA. 2009.
articles.finding: No mortality benefit overall, with a trend toward benefit in severe hypoxemia.

articles.title: CESAR: referral for ECMO in severe respiratory failure
articles.citation: Peek GJ, et al. Lancet. 2009.
articles.finding: Transfer to an ECMO center improved survival without severe disability at 6 months. Only 75% of the ECMO arm received ECMO.

articles.title: EOLIA: ECMO for severe ARDS
articles.citation: Combes A, et al. N Engl J Med. 2018.
articles.finding: 60-day mortality 35% with early ECMO versus 46% with conventional care, not significant, with 28% crossover to rescue ECMO.

articles.title: OSCAR: high-frequency oscillation in ARDS
articles.citation: Young D, et al. N Engl J Med. 2013.
articles.finding: HFOV made no difference to 30-day mortality.

articles.title: OSCILLATE: high-frequency oscillation in early ARDS
articles.citation: Ferguson ND, et al. N Engl J Med. 2013.
articles.finding: Stopped early. HFOV increased in-hospital mortality (47% versus 35%).

articles.title: 3CPO: NIV in acute cardiogenic pulmonary edema
articles.citation: Gray A, et al. N Engl J Med. 2008.
articles.finding: CPAP and NIPPV relieved dyspnea and acidosis faster than oxygen alone but did not reduce 7-day mortality or intubation.

articles.title: Early NIV after extubation in hypercapnic patients
articles.citation: Ferrer M, et al. Lancet. 2009.
articles.finding: Preventive NIV in chronic respiratory disease with hypercapnia during the SBT reduced post-extubation respiratory failure and 90-day mortality.

articles.title: NIV for respiratory failure after extubation
articles.citation: Esteban A, et al. N Engl J Med. 2004.
articles.finding: NIV for established post-extubation failure did not prevent reintubation and increased ICU mortality, largely by delaying reintubation.

articles.title: NIVAS: NIV after abdominal surgery
articles.citation: Jaber S, et al. JAMA. 2016.
articles.finding: NIV for hypoxemic respiratory failure after abdominal surgery reduced reintubation within 7 days.

articles.title: BiPOP: high-flow oxygen versus BiPAP after cardiothoracic surgery
articles.citation: Stephan F, et al. JAMA. 2015.
articles.finding: High-flow nasal oxygen was noninferior to BiPAP for treatment failure in hypoxemic patients after cardiothoracic surgery.

articles.title: FLORALI: high-flow oxygen in hypoxemic respiratory failure
articles.citation: Frat JP, et al. N Engl J Med. 2015.
articles.finding: No difference in intubation overall, but HFNC had lower 90-day mortality than standard oxygen or NIV.

articles.title: HFNC versus NIV after extubation in high-risk patients
articles.citation: Hernandez G, et al. JAMA. 2016.
articles.finding: High-flow nasal cannula was noninferior to NIV for reintubation and post-extubation respiratory failure.

articles.title: HFNC versus conventional oxygen after extubation in low-risk patients
articles.citation: Hernandez G, et al. JAMA. 2016.
articles.finding: High-flow nasal cannula reduced reintubation within 72 hours compared with conventional oxygen.

articles.title: Four methods of weaning from mechanical ventilation
articles.citation: Esteban A, et al. N Engl J Med. 1995.
articles.finding: Once-daily spontaneous breathing trials weaned patients faster than pressure support or SIMV.

articles.title: Methylprednisolone to prevent post-extubation laryngeal edema
articles.citation: Francois B, et al. Lancet. 2007.
articles.finding: Methylprednisolone started 12 hours before planned extubation reduced laryngeal edema and reintubation.

articles.title: Rapid shallow breathing index
articles.citation: Yang KL, Tobin MJ. N Engl J Med. 1991.
articles.finding: Frequency to tidal volume ratio of 105 or less during a spontaneous breathing trial predicted successful weaning.

articles.title: TracMan: early versus late tracheostomy
articles.citation: Young D, et al. JAMA. 2013.
articles.finding: Tracheostomy at day 4 versus day 10 did not change 30-day mortality, and clinicians predicted the need for prolonged ventilation poorly.

articles.title: Early versus late tracheotomy and pneumonia
articles.citation: Terragni PP, et al. JAMA. 2010.
articles.finding: Tracheotomy at 6 to 8 days versus 13 to 15 days did not significantly reduce ventilator-associated pneumonia.

articles.title: Oxygen-ICU: conservative versus conventional oxygen
articles.citation: Girardis M, et al. JAMA. 2016.
articles.finding: Targeting PaO2 70 to 100 mm Hg lowered ICU mortality in a single-center trial stopped early.

articles.title: SO-COOL: avoiding hyperoxemia on cardiopulmonary bypass
articles.citation: McGuinness SP, et al. Anesthesiology. 2016.
articles.finding: Avoiding hyperoxemia during bypass did not reduce acute kidney injury after cardiac surgery.

articles.title: TracMan: early versus late tracheostomy
articles.citation: Young D, et al. JAMA. 2013.
articles.finding: Tracheostomy at day 4 versus day 10 did not change 30-day mortality, and clinicians predicted the need for prolonged ventilation poorly.

articles.session: Sepsis: early goal-directed therapy and fluids
articles.title: CLASSIC: restrictive intravenous fluid in septic shock
articles.citation: Meyhoff TS, et al. N Engl J Med. 2022.
articles.finding: Restricting IV fluid in the ICU after initial resuscitation did not change 90-day mortality.

articles.session: Sepsis: early goal-directed therapy and fluids
articles.title: CLOVERS: restrictive versus liberal fluids in sepsis-induced hypotension
articles.citation: Shapiro NI, et al. N Engl J Med. 2023.
articles.finding: Early vasopressors with restricted fluid versus liberal fluid: no difference in 90-day mortality.

articles.session: Sepsis: early goal-directed therapy and fluids
articles.title: ProCESS: protocol-based care for early septic shock
articles.citation: ProCESS Investigators. N Engl J Med. 2014.
articles.finding: Protocolized EGDT, protocolized standard therapy, and usual care had the same 60-day mortality.

articles.session: Sepsis: early goal-directed therapy and fluids
articles.title: Rivers: early goal-directed therapy
articles.citation: Rivers E, et al. N Engl J Med. 2001.
articles.finding: Single-center trial in which EGDT reduced in-hospital mortality from 46.5% to 30.5%. Not reproduced by ProCESS, ARISE, or ProMISe.

articles.title: ANDROMEDA-SHOCK: capillary refill versus lactate targets
articles.citation: Hernandez G, et al. JAMA. 2019.
articles.finding: Peripheral perfusion-targeted resuscitation did not significantly reduce 28-day mortality (34.9% versus 43.4%) but produced less organ dysfunction.

articles.title: LACTATE: early lactate-guided therapy
articles.citation: Jansen TC, et al. Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2010.
articles.finding: Targeting a 20% lactate decrease every 2 hours reduced adjusted in-hospital mortality.

articles.title: OPTIMISE: cardiac output-guided hemodynamic therapy
articles.citation: Pearse RM, et al. JAMA. 2014.
articles.finding: A perioperative cardiac output-guided algorithm did not significantly reduce complications; the updated meta-analysis favored it.

articles.title: RELIEF: restrictive versus liberal fluids in major abdominal surgery
articles.citation: Myles PS, et al. N Engl J Med. 2018.
articles.finding: A restrictive regimen did not improve disability-free survival and increased acute kidney injury.

articles.title: ADRENAL: hydrocortisone in septic shock
articles.citation: Venkatesh B, et al. N Engl J Med. 2018.
articles.finding: Continuous hydrocortisone did not reduce 90-day mortality but shortened shock, ventilation, and ICU stay.

articles.title: APROCCHSS: hydrocortisone plus fludrocortisone
articles.citation: Annane D, et al. N Engl J Med. 2018.
articles.finding: Hydrocortisone with fludrocortisone reduced 90-day mortality in septic shock from 49% to 43%.

articles.title: CORTICUS: hydrocortisone in septic shock
articles.citation: Sprung CL, et al. N Engl J Med. 2008.
articles.finding: Hydrocortisone hastened shock reversal but did not improve 28-day mortality, regardless of corticotropin response.

articles.title: HYPRESS: hydrocortisone in severe sepsis without shock
articles.citation: Keh D, et al. JAMA. 2016.
articles.finding: Hydrocortisone did not prevent progression to septic shock.

articles.title: ATHOS-3: angiotensin II for vasodilatory shock
articles.citation: Khanna A, et al. N Engl J Med. 2017.
articles.finding: Angiotensin II raised MAP in catecholamine-resistant vasodilatory shock. Not powered for mortality.

articles.title: Esmolol for heart rate control in septic shock
articles.citation: Morelli A, et al. JAMA. 2013.
articles.finding: Single-center trial in which esmolol to a heart rate of 80 to 94 reduced 28-day mortality from 80.5% to 49.4%. Treat the control mortality with suspicion.

articles.title: SOAP II: dopamine versus norepinephrine in shock
articles.citation: De Backer D, et al. N Engl J Med. 2010.
articles.finding: No overall mortality difference, but dopamine caused more arrhythmias and higher mortality in cardiogenic shock.

articles.title: VASST: vasopressin versus norepinephrine
articles.citation: Russell JA, et al. N Engl J Med. 2008.
articles.finding: Adding low-dose vasopressin did not reduce 28-day mortality overall; a possible benefit appeared in less severe shock.

articles.session: Sepsis: blood pressure targets and activated protein C
articles.title: LeoPARDS: levosimendan in sepsis
articles.citation: Gordon AC, et al. N Engl J Med. 2016.
articles.finding: Levosimendan did not reduce organ dysfunction and caused more supraventricular tachyarrhythmia.

articles.session: Sepsis: blood pressure targets and activated protein C
articles.title: PROWESS-SHOCK: drotrecogin alfa in septic shock
articles.citation: Ranieri VM, et al. N Engl J Med. 2012.
articles.finding: No mortality benefit. The drug was withdrawn from the market.

articles.session: Sepsis: blood pressure targets and activated protein C
articles.title: PROWESS: drotrecogin alfa in severe sepsis
articles.citation: Bernard GR, et al. N Engl J Med. 2001.
articles.finding: Recombinant activated protein C reduced 28-day mortality from 30.8% to 24.7%, with more serious bleeding.

articles.session: Sepsis: blood pressure targets and activated protein C
articles.title: Risks and benefits of activated protein C: Sounding Board
articles.citation: Warren HS, et al. N Engl J Med. 2002.
articles.finding: The FDA reviewers' account of the PROWESS protocol change midway through the trial and why the result should be read cautiously.

articles.session: Sepsis: blood pressure targets and activated protein C
articles.title: SEPSISPAM: high versus low blood pressure target
articles.citation: Asfar P, et al. N Engl J Med. 2014.
articles.finding: MAP 80 to 85 versus 65 to 70: no mortality difference, more atrial fibrillation, less renal replacement in chronic hypertension.

articles.title: FOCUS: transfusion after hip fracture surgery
articles.citation: Carson JL, et al. N Engl J Med. 2011.
articles.finding: Liberal (Hb under 10) versus restrictive (symptoms or Hb under 8) in high-risk elderly patients: no difference in death or walking.

articles.title: TRICC: transfusion requirements in critical care
articles.citation: Hebert PC, et al. N Engl J Med. 1999.
articles.finding: Hb 7 versus 10 threshold: noninferior overall, and lower mortality in younger and less ill patients.

articles.title: TRISS: transfusion threshold in septic shock
articles.citation: Holst LB, et al. N Engl J Med. 2014.
articles.finding: Hb 7 versus 9 in septic shock: same 90-day mortality with half the transfusions.

articles.title: Transfusion strategies in acute upper GI bleeding
articles.citation: Villanueva C, et al. N Engl J Med. 2013.
articles.finding: A restrictive threshold of 7 improved 6-week survival and reduced rebleeding compared with 9.

articles.title: TITRe2: transfusion after cardiac surgery
articles.citation: Murphy GJ, et al. N Engl J Med. 2015.
articles.finding: Hb under 7.5 versus under 9: no difference in infection or ischemic events; 90-day mortality was higher in the restrictive arm as a secondary outcome.

articles.title: TRACS: transfusion after cardiac surgery
articles.citation: Hajjar LA, et al. JAMA. 2010.
articles.finding: Hematocrit 24% versus 30% was noninferior for a composite of death and severe morbidity.

articles.title: TRICS III: restrictive transfusion in cardiac surgery
articles.citation: Mazer CD, et al. N Engl J Med. 2017.
articles.finding: Hb under 7.5 was noninferior to Hb under 9.5 for death, MI, stroke, and new dialysis.

articles.title: TRICS III: six-month outcomes
articles.citation: Mazer CD, et al. N Engl J Med. 2018.
articles.finding: Noninferiority of the restrictive strategy persisted at 6 months.

articles.session: Transfusion: age of blood and trauma resuscitation
articles.title: PAMPer: prehospital plasma in hemorrhagic shock
articles.citation: Sperry JL, et al. N Engl J Med. 2018.
articles.finding: Prehospital thawed plasma during air transport reduced 30-day mortality.

articles.session: Transfusion: age of blood and trauma resuscitation
articles.title: PROPPR: 1:1:1 versus 1:1:2 in severe trauma
articles.citation: Holcomb JB, et al. JAMA. 2015.
articles.finding: No difference in 24-hour or 30-day mortality; 1:1:1 achieved hemostasis more often with fewer deaths from exsanguination.

articles.session: Transfusion: age of blood and trauma resuscitation
articles.title: TRANSFUSE: age of red cells
articles.citation: Cooper DJ, et al. N Engl J Med. 2017.
articles.finding: Freshest available versus standard-issue red cells: no difference in 90-day mortality.

articles.title: ABC: paired sedation and ventilator weaning
articles.citation: Girard TD, et al. Lancet. 2008.
articles.finding: Daily awakening trial paired with a breathing trial increased ventilator-free days and reduced 1-year mortality.

articles.title: Daily interruption of sedative infusions
articles.citation: Kress JP, et al. N Engl J Med. 2000.
articles.finding: Daily sedation interruption shortened mechanical ventilation and ICU stay.

articles.title: No sedation for ventilated patients
articles.citation: Strom T, et al. Lancet. 2010.
articles.finding: A protocol of no sedation with morphine boluses increased ventilator-free days and shortened ICU stay.

articles.title: SLEAP: daily interruption with protocolized sedation
articles.citation: Mehta S, et al. JAMA. 2012.
articles.finding: Adding daily interruption to nurse-driven protocolized sedation did not shorten ventilation and increased sedative doses and nursing workload.

articles.title: Lorazepam as a risk factor for delirium
articles.citation: Pandharipande P, et al. Anesthesiology. 2006.
articles.finding: Lorazepam was an independent, dose-related risk factor for transitioning to delirium.

articles.title: MENDS2: dexmedetomidine versus propofol in sepsis
articles.citation: Hughes CG, et al. N Engl J Med. 2021.
articles.finding: No difference in days alive without delirium or coma, ventilator-free days, or 90-day mortality.

articles.title: MENDS: dexmedetomidine versus lorazepam
articles.citation: Pandharipande PP, et al. JAMA. 2007.
articles.finding: Dexmedetomidine produced more days alive without delirium or coma than lorazepam.

articles.title: MIDEX and PRODEX: dexmedetomidine versus midazolam or propofol
articles.citation: Jakob SM, et al. JAMA. 2012.
articles.finding: Dexmedetomidine was noninferior for time at target sedation and shortened ventilation compared with midazolam.

articles.session: Delirium: assessment scales and early mobility
articles.title: CAM-ICU validation
articles.citation: Ely EW, et al. JAMA. 2001.
articles.finding: The Confusion Assessment Method for the ICU was valid and reliable in ventilated patients.

articles.session: Delirium: assessment scales and early mobility
articles.title: Delirium as a predictor of mortality
articles.citation: Ely EW, et al. JAMA. 2004.
articles.finding: Delirium independently predicted 6-month mortality and longer hospital stay in ventilated patients.

articles.session: Delirium: assessment scales and early mobility
articles.title: Early physical and occupational therapy
articles.citation: Schweickert WD, et al. Lancet. 2009.
articles.finding: PT and OT during daily sedation interruption improved return to independent function and shortened delirium.

articles.session: Delirium: assessment scales and early mobility
articles.title: RASS validation
articles.citation: Sessler CN, et al. Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2002.
articles.finding: The Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale was valid and reliable in adult ICU patients.

articles.title: Editorial: preventing delirium in the ICU
articles.citation: Delaney A, et al. JAMA. 2018.
articles.finding: Accompanying editorial to REDUCE on why prophylactic haloperidol failed and what nonpharmacologic prevention offers.

articles.title: Hope-ICU: haloperidol for delirium
articles.citation: Page VJ, et al. Lancet Respir Med. 2013.
articles.finding: Intravenous haloperidol did not change days free of delirium and coma.

articles.title: MIND-USA: haloperidol and ziprasidone for delirium
articles.citation: Girard TD, et al. N Engl J Med. 2018.
articles.finding: Neither antipsychotic changed days alive without delirium or coma.

articles.title: REDUCE: prophylactic haloperidol
articles.citation: van den Boogaard M, et al. JAMA. 2018.
articles.finding: Prophylactic haloperidol in high-risk patients did not improve 28-day survival.

articles.title: ALBIOS: albumin replacement in severe sepsis
articles.citation: Caironi P, et al. N Engl J Med. 2014.
articles.finding: Albumin to a target of 30 g/L did not improve survival; a post hoc signal favored it in septic shock.

articles.title: Furosemide with or without albumin in acute lung injury
articles.citation: Martin GS, et al. Crit Care Med. 2005.
articles.finding: Albumin plus furosemide improved oxygenation and hemodynamics in hypoproteinemic patients with ALI.

articles.title: SAFE: albumin versus saline
articles.citation: Finfer S, et al. N Engl J Med. 2004.
articles.finding: 4% albumin and saline produced the same 28-day mortality. A later analysis found harm with albumin in traumatic brain injury.

articles.session: Fluids: colloids, CVP, and balanced crystalloids
articles.title: CRISTAL: colloids versus crystalloids in hypovolemic shock
articles.citation: Annane D, et al. JAMA. 2013.
articles.finding: No 28-day mortality difference; 90-day mortality favored colloids as a secondary outcome. Open label.

articles.session: Fluids: colloids, CVP, and balanced crystalloids
articles.title: Does CVP predict fluid responsiveness?
articles.citation: Marik PE, Cavallazzi R. Crit Care Med. 2013.
articles.finding: Updated meta-analysis: central venous pressure does not predict fluid responsiveness.

articles.session: Fluids: colloids, CVP, and balanced crystalloids
articles.title: SALT-ED: balanced crystalloids in noncritically ill adults
articles.citation: Self WH, et al. N Engl J Med. 2018.
articles.finding: Balanced crystalloids in the emergency department reduced major adverse kidney events at 30 days.

articles.session: Fluids: colloids, CVP, and balanced crystalloids
articles.title: SMART: balanced crystalloids in critically ill adults
articles.citation: Semler MW, et al. N Engl J Med. 2018.
articles.finding: Balanced crystalloids reduced major adverse kidney events at 30 days compared with saline.

articles.title: Chloride-liberal versus chloride-restrictive fluids
articles.citation: Yunos NM, et al. JAMA. 2012.
articles.finding: Before-and-after study: restricting chloride-rich fluids was associated with less AKI and renal replacement therapy.

articles.title: Chloride-restrictive fluids and AKI: extended analysis
articles.citation: Yunos NM, et al. Intensive Care Med. 2015.
articles.finding: The reduction in AKI with a chloride-restrictive strategy persisted over a longer follow-up period.

articles.title: PLUS: balanced multielectrolyte solution versus saline
articles.citation: Finfer S, et al. N Engl J Med. 2022.
articles.finding: Plasma-Lyte 148 and saline produced the same 90-day mortality.

articles.title: SPLIT: buffered crystalloid versus saline
articles.citation: Young P, et al. JAMA. 2015.
articles.finding: Plasma-Lyte 148 did not reduce acute kidney injury compared with saline.

articles.session: Fluids: hydroxyethyl starch, insulin, and contrast
articles.title: 6S: hydroxyethyl starch in severe sepsis
articles.citation: Perner A, et al. N Engl J Med. 2012.
articles.finding: HES 130/0.42 increased 90-day mortality and renal replacement therapy compared with Ringer's acetate.

articles.session: Fluids: hydroxyethyl starch, insulin, and contrast
articles.title: CHEST: hydroxyethyl starch versus saline
articles.citation: Myburgh JA, et al. N Engl J Med. 2012.
articles.finding: HES 130/0.4 did not change 90-day mortality but increased renal replacement therapy.

articles.session: Fluids: hydroxyethyl starch, insulin, and contrast
articles.title: PRESERVE: bicarbonate and acetylcysteine before angiography
articles.citation: Weisbord SD, et al. N Engl J Med. 2018.
articles.finding: Neither sodium bicarbonate nor acetylcysteine prevented death, dialysis, or persistent kidney impairment after angiography.

articles.session: Fluids: hydroxyethyl starch, insulin, and contrast
articles.title: VISEP: intensive insulin and pentastarch in severe sepsis
articles.citation: Brunkhorst FM, et al. N Engl J Med. 2008.
articles.finding: Intensive insulin caused hypoglycemia without benefit, and pentastarch increased acute kidney injury and renal replacement.

articles.session: Renal: timing of renal replacement therapy
articles.title: AKIKI: early versus delayed renal replacement therapy
articles.citation: Gaudry S, et al. N Engl J Med. 2016.
articles.finding: No mortality difference, and half of the delayed group never required dialysis.

articles.session: Renal: timing of renal replacement therapy
articles.title: ELAIN: early versus delayed renal replacement therapy
articles.citation: Zarbock A, et al. JAMA. 2016.
articles.finding: Single-center trial in which early initiation at KDIGO stage 2 reduced 90-day mortality. Not reproduced in AKIKI or STARRT-AKI.

articles.session: Renal: timing of renal replacement therapy
articles.title: PICARD: diuretics in acute renal failure
articles.citation: Mehta RL, et al. JAMA. 2002.
articles.finding: Diuretic use in acute renal failure was associated with higher mortality and nonrecovery of renal function.

articles.session: Renal: timing of renal replacement therapy
articles.title: STARRT-AKI: timing of renal replacement therapy
articles.citation: Bagshaw SM, et al. N Engl J Med. 2020.
articles.finding: Accelerated initiation did not reduce 90-day mortality and increased dialysis dependence among survivors.

articles.title: 3SITES: central venous catheter insertion site
articles.citation: Parienti JJ, et al. N Engl J Med. 2015.
articles.finding: Subclavian had the fewest bloodstream infections and thromboses but the most pneumothoraces.

articles.title: Chlorhexidine sponges and dressing change frequency
articles.citation: Timsit JF, et al. JAMA. 2009.
articles.finding: Chlorhexidine-impregnated sponges reduced catheter-related infections; changing dressings every 7 days was noninferior to every 3.

articles.title: Keystone ICU: an intervention to decrease catheter-related bloodstream infections
articles.citation: Pronovost P, et al. N Engl J Med. 2006.
articles.finding: A five-item checklist across Michigan ICUs cut catheter-related bloodstream infections by two thirds.

articles.title: Matching Michigan: CLABSI program in England
articles.citation: Bion J, et al. BMJ Qual Saf. 2013.
articles.finding: Central line infections fell during the program, but the decline had begun before the intervention, complicating attribution.

articles.title: Daily chlorhexidine bathing
articles.citation: Climo MW, et al. N Engl J Med. 2013.
articles.finding: Daily chlorhexidine bathing reduced MDRO acquisition and hospital-acquired bloodstream infections.

articles.title: Duodenal infusion of donor feces for recurrent C. difficile
articles.citation: van Nood E, et al. N Engl J Med. 2013.
articles.finding: Fecal microbiota transplantation resolved recurrent C. difficile in 81% versus 31% with vancomycin; stopped early.

articles.title: R-GNOSIS: decontamination strategies in ventilated patients
articles.citation: Wittekamp BH, et al. JAMA. 2018.
articles.finding: In low-resistance ICUs, chlorhexidine mouthwash, SOD, and SDD did not reduce bloodstream infections with resistant organisms.

articles.title: REDUCE MRSA: targeted versus universal decolonization
articles.citation: Huang SS, et al. N Engl J Med. 2013.
articles.finding: Universal decolonization with chlorhexidine and mupirocin beat screening and isolation for MRSA clinical isolates and all-cause bloodstream infection.

articles.title: 8 versus 15 days of antibiotics for VAP
articles.citation: Chastre J, et al. JAMA. 2003.
articles.finding: Eight days was as effective as 15, with more recurrences when the pathogen was a nonfermenting gram-negative bacillus.

articles.title: PRORATA: procalcitonin to reduce antibiotic exposure
articles.citation: Bouadma L, et al. Lancet. 2010.
articles.finding: Procalcitonin guidance cut antibiotic days with noninferior mortality.

articles.title: ProACT: procalcitonin-guided antibiotics for lower respiratory tract infection
articles.citation: Huang DT, et al. N Engl J Med. 2018.
articles.finding: In US emergency departments, procalcitonin guidance did not reduce antibiotic use.

articles.title: Continuous versus intermittent beta-lactam infusion
articles.citation: Roberts JA, et al. Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2016.
articles.finding: Individual patient data meta-analysis: continuous infusion was associated with lower hospital mortality in severe sepsis.

articles.title: HEAT: acetaminophen for fever in suspected infection
articles.citation: Young P, et al. N Engl J Med. 2015.
articles.finding: Early acetaminophen for fever did not change ICU-free days.

articles.title: Inappropriate initial antimicrobial therapy in septic shock
articles.citation: Kumar A, et al. Chest. 2009.
articles.finding: Initial antimicrobial therapy that did not cover the pathogen was associated with a fivefold reduction in survival.

articles.title: STOP-IT: short-course antibiotics for intraabdominal infection
articles.citation: Sawyer RG, et al. N Engl J Med. 2015.
articles.finding: About 4 days of antibiotics after source control was equivalent to a longer course.

articles.title: HACA: mild hypothermia after cardiac arrest
articles.citation: Hypothermia after Cardiac Arrest Study Group. N Engl J Med. 2002.
articles.finding: Cooling to 32 to 34 degrees after out-of-hospital VF arrest improved favorable neurologic outcome and mortality.

articles.title: HYPO-ECMO: moderate hypothermia on VA ECMO
articles.citation: Levy B, et al. JAMA. 2022.
articles.finding: Hypothermia to 33 to 34 degrees in cardiogenic shock on VA ECMO did not significantly reduce 30-day mortality.

articles.title: POLAR: prophylactic hypothermia in severe TBI
articles.citation: Cooper DJ, et al. JAMA. 2018.
articles.finding: Early sustained hypothermia did not improve neurologic outcome at 6 months.

articles.title: TTH48: targeted temperature management for 48 versus 24 hours
articles.citation: Kirkegaard H, et al. JAMA. 2017.
articles.finding: Extending TTM at 33 degrees to 48 hours did not improve 6-month neurologic outcome.

articles.title: TTM: 33 versus 36 degrees after cardiac arrest
articles.citation: Nielsen N, et al. N Engl J Med. 2013.
articles.finding: No difference in mortality or neurologic outcome between 33 and 36 degrees.

articles.title: BEAM: bougie versus stylet in difficult airways
articles.citation: Driver BE, et al. JAMA. 2018.
articles.finding: Bougie first improved first-attempt success in emergency intubations with difficult airway features.

articles.title: CAAM: bag-mask ventilation versus intubation during CPR
articles.citation: Jabre P, et al. JAMA. 2018.
articles.finding: Noninferiority of bag-mask ventilation for 28-day favorable neurologic outcome was inconclusive.

articles.title: MACMAN: video versus direct laryngoscopy in the ICU
articles.citation: Lascarrou JB, et al. JAMA. 2017.
articles.finding: Video laryngoscopy did not improve first-pass success and was associated with more severe life-threatening complications.

articles.title: PreVent: bag-mask ventilation during intubation
articles.citation: Casey JD, et al. N Engl J Med. 2019.
articles.finding: Bag-mask ventilation between induction and laryngoscopy halved severe hypoxemia without increasing aspiration.

articles.title: Prehospital advanced airway management in cardiac arrest
articles.citation: Hasegawa K, et al. JAMA. 2013.
articles.finding: In a Japanese registry, prehospital advanced airways were associated with worse neurologic outcome than bag-mask ventilation.

articles.session: Drugs and ECPR in cardiac arrest
articles.title: Adrenaline in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: meta-analysis
articles.citation: Lin S, et al. Resuscitation. 2014.
articles.finding: Epinephrine improved return of spontaneous circulation but not survival to discharge or neurologic outcome.

articles.session: Drugs and ECPR in cardiac arrest
articles.title: Early epinephrine in shockable in-hospital arrest
articles.citation: Andersen LW, et al. BMJ. 2016.
articles.finding: Epinephrine within 2 minutes of the first defibrillation was associated with lower survival to discharge.

articles.session: Drugs and ECPR in cardiac arrest
articles.title: INCEPTION: early extracorporeal CPR
articles.citation: Suverein MM, et al. N Engl J Med. 2023.
articles.finding: ECPR for refractory out-of-hospital arrest did not improve 30-day survival with favorable neurologic outcome.

articles.session: Drugs and ECPR in cardiac arrest
articles.title: PARAMEDIC2: epinephrine in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest
articles.citation: Perkins GD, et al. N Engl J Med. 2018.
articles.finding: Epinephrine improved 30-day survival (3.2% versus 2.4%) without improving favorable neurologic outcome.

articles.session: Drugs and ECPR in cardiac arrest
articles.title: Vasopressin, steroids, and epinephrine in in-hospital arrest
articles.citation: Mentzelopoulos SD, et al. JAMA. 2013.
articles.finding: The VSE combination improved survival with favorable neurologic status compared with epinephrine alone.
